narrative:
The model determined that you have a 56% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeds the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

Three pieces of information about you weighed most heavily in this outcome. By far the strongest factor was your credit history showing no prior credits or all accounts paid. While this category is rare among approved applicants (only 1%), the model interpreted it as a lack of proven reliability in managing debt, strongly pushing your prediction toward bad credit risk.

The second most important factor was the status of your checking account, which sits between 0 and 200 DM. This is less favorable than the none or higher-balance accounts that most approved borrowers have, adding further pressure toward denial.

Third, the loan amount you requested (4,280 DM) worked in your favor because it was not excessively large. However, this positive influence was not enough to overcome the concerns raised by your credit history and checking account status.

Taken together, these factors led the model to conclude that the risk was too high. To improve your chances on a future application, focus first on building a consistent record of repaying credit accounts on time. Even a few successfully managed smaller loans or credit cards could demonstrate reliability and significantly strengthen your profile. Consider reapplying once you have established that positive payment history.
